title: Forecast-driven reservation scheduling & autoscale ops roadmap (Q3 slice)
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Build a data-driven reservation scheduling system and accompanying autoscale operational playbook for Dedicated pools. This Q3 slice focuses on turning short-term demand forecasts into reservation adjustments and warm-pool targets so we can reduce idle commit costs while preserving SLOs. Background: reservation hedging and warm pools have reduced latency spikes, but manual tuning and coarse time windows cause both overcommitment and late capacity shortfalls. This initiative bridges forecasting, autoscaler policy, and operator runbooks. Goals: 1) Implement a forecast->reservation pipeline to suggest reservation deltas for next 48h windows; 2) Add an autoscale policy tier that accepts forecast-driven targets with guarded rollback rules; 3) Deliver operator runbooks and canary dashboards so SREs can observe and override in real time. Success metrics: cost/unit reduction (target 8% on prewarmed pools), 99.9% latency SLO compliance during scale events, <1 escalated incident per quarter for autoscale-related adjustments. Out of scope: full multi-region automatic commit placement (left for a future phase).
tasks: Instrument historic pooling and request traces to create demand time-series (ENG-5187)
Prototype short-term (24-72h) demand forecast model and evaluate accuracy against Q1-Q2 data
Define reservation suggestion schema and validation rules for safety (rollback windows, min/max deltas)
Implement controller that converts approved suggestions into reservation API calls with audit logging
Add autoscale policy mode 'forecast-suggest' to Dedicated autoscaler with feature flag
Create Grafana canary dashboard and alerting for forecast vs actual occupancy and cost delta
Write operator runbook: validate suggestions, manual override, emergency rollback
Run canary in single non-production pool for 3 weeks, iterate, then expand to two low-risk production pools

acceptance_criteria: Forecast pipeline produces suggestions with documented accuracy and bias metrics for 24/48/72h horizons
Controller applies reservation adjustments via API and logs an audit event for each change
Autoscaler 'forecast-suggest' mode respects safety rules (max delta, cool-down, manual hold)
Canary dashboard shows forecast vs actual with clear alert thresholds and SRE sign-off
Operator runbook published and on-call trained; two dry-run exercises completed
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-committing reservations causes unnecessary cost. Mitigation: Strict max-delta and budget-aware guardrails; manual approval toggle for high-cost pools.
Risk: Forecast underestimation causes latency breaches. Mitigation: Use asymmetric loss to favor overprovisioning and keep emergency auto-fallback to burst pools.
Risk: Commit API rate limits or quotas. Mitigation: Batch reservation changes and add retry/backoff logic in controller.
open_questions: Q1: Should suggestions be auto-applied for low-risk pools or always require operator approval? (tradeoff: speed vs safety)
Q2: Which cost metric should be used to gate automated apply? (gross reserved spend vs normalized $/token)
Q3: How do we attribute cost savings back to customer accounts for commercial reporting?
notes: Decision: Start with suggestion-first (non-auto) apply for first two canary pools to collect operator feedback.
Tradeoff: Tighter guardrails reduce risk but also limit cost upside; we prioritize SLO preservation for now.
Follow-up: If canary meets metrics for two consecutive cycles, revisit auto-apply for low-cost pools in phase 2.
